name: ls-qpack
baseline: nghttp3 (QPACK encoder compression ratio); nghttp2/nginx Huffman coder (shared HPACK/QPACK Huffman alphabet)
workload: Huffman encode/decode of real HTTP header samples (short header, Facebook x-fb-debug header, paragraph-length text) run 1e5-1e9 iterations (litespeedtech/benchmarks repo); separately, QPACK compression ratio (compressed bytes / QIF source bytes) on a captured Facebook response header trace, compared directly against nghttp3's QPACK encoder.
claimed_speedup: Huffman decoder 1.15-1.96x faster than nginx's decoder; Huffman encoder 2.37-5.77x faster than nghttp2's encoder (also 1.11-2.12x vs nginx, 1.18-3.59x vs h2o); QPACK compression ratio 0.16-0.18 vs nghttp3's 0.21-0.39 (lower=better) on a Facebook response header trace (derived from page data: roughly 1.3-2.2x more compact).
stars_or_usage: 86 stars; used in OpenLiteSpeed, LiteSpeed Web Server and Web ADC
tradeoffs: Vanilla C99 with a lower-level API (struct lsxpack_header); needs wrapping for higher-level languages (Go/Python/Rust/TS/Ruby wrappers exist but are separately maintained third-party projects).
caveats: The 2019 Huffman timing posts compare against nginx's and nghttp2's Huffman coder, not nghttp3 directly, and state no compiler flags or CPU model, which caps the timing claim at tier C. The 2021 QPACK-ratio post does name nghttp3 directly but measures compression ratio (bytes on the wire), not runtime speed, and is a first-party, non-replicated comparison.
found_via: Blogs: seed query 'QUIC performance benchmark blog' led to h2o/quicly and other QUIC libs; ls-qpack README links to blog.litespeedtech.com/2019/10/03/fast-huffman-encoder/, /2019/09/16/fast-huffman-decoder/, and /2021/04/05/qpack-mnemonic-technique/, all opened directly.

name: mvfst
baseline: HTTP/2 over TCP (Facebook's prior production transport stack)
workload: Production staged rollout of QUIC/HTTP-3 (built on mvfst + Proxygen) across the Facebook and Instagram apps for dynamic API requests and video delivery, at global scale, eventually covering more than 75% of Facebook's internet traffic.
claimed_speedup: vs HTTP/2: 6% fewer request errors, 20% lower tail latency, 5% smaller response headers on dynamic requests; on video: mean time between rebuffering improved up to 22%, video error count down 8%, rate of video stalls down 20%.
stars_or_usage: 1.66k stars; powers QUIC/HTTP-3 for the Facebook and Instagram apps
tradeoffs: C++14/17, tightly coupled to Facebook's Proxygen and Folly; the reported gains come from a live production A/B rollout, not a controlled lab benchmark, so they mix client population and network-condition effects with pure protocol-implementation speed.
caveats: First-party production A/B numbers with no fixed workload, hardware, or compiler/flags stated, so tier is capped at C. The comparison baseline is 'HTTP/2 over TCP', not one of the category's named baselines (msquic/quiche/nghttp3) directly, so baseline_in_list=false.
found_via: Blogs: engineering.fb.com search for 'mvfst quic' -> 'How Facebook is bringing QUIC to billions' (2020-10-21), opened directly.
